sentences.text: (S.B.CIVIL WRIT PETITION NO.3459/08)
HON'BLE MR.JUSTICE SANGEET LODHA Mr.Rajesh Joshi, for the petitioner.
Dr.Pratistha Dave, Additional Government Counsel.

1. This writ petition is directed against notice dated 15.5.08 issued by the Deputy Secretary, Local Self Department, Government of Rajasthan, initiating proceedings under Section 63 of Rajasthan Municipalities Act, 1959 ( for short "the Act") for removal of the petitioner as member of Municipal Board, Pipar City.

2. The proceedings for removal has been initiated on the ground that the cognizance for offences under Sections 7(i) (ii)
(vi)/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 ( 'PFA Act') having been taken by the court of competent jurisdiction, on a complaint lodged against the petitioner, he has incurred disqualification under Section 26(i)(c) of the Act.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that as per provisions of Section 26(i)(c) of the Act, a person incurs disqualification for being chosen as or for being a member of the Municipal Board,
who has been convicted for offence under the AMRA RAM BHATI VS. STATE OF RAJASTHAN &
ORS.
(S.B.CIVIL WRIT PETITION NO.3459/08) PFA Act and therefore, merely, on account of cognizance being taken for offences under the PFA Act, no proceedings could have been initiated against the petitioner for his removal as member of the Municipal Board.

Learned Additional Government Counsel submits that the tenure of the petitioner as member has already come to an end and therefore, even otherwise, the question of continuing with the proceedings for removal does not arise.
5. I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.

6. Indisputably, as per the provisions of Section 63 (1)(c) of the Act, member of a Municipal Board is liable to be removed on the ground that after his election, he has incurred any of the disqualification mentioned in Section 18 or Section 26 or has ceased to fulfill the requirement of Section 24.
7. Section 26 which deals with the general disqualification for members and as per clause (i-c)
thereof, a person notwithstanding that he is otherwise qualified shall be disqualified for being chosen as of or for being as member of the Board who has been convicted of an offence under PFA Act.
8.

In this view of the matter, no proceedings in terms of the provisions of Section 63 (1)(c) could be initiated for removal of AMRA RAM BHATI VS. STATE OF RAJASTHAN & ORS.
(S.B.CIVIL WRIT PETITION NO.3459/08) the petitioner merely because, the cognizance of the offences under the PFA Act has been taken by the criminal court of competent jurisdiction on a complaint being filed against the petitioner.

entities.text: AMRA RAM BHATI VS. STATE OF RAJASTHAN & ORS
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. Thus, the impugned notice issued by the State Government initiating proceeding against the petitioner for his removal as member of the Municipal Board, Pipar City in purported exercise of the power conferred under Section 63 is ex facie without jurisdiction.
10. In the result, the petition succeeds, it is hereby allowed.
The impugned notice dated 15.5.08 issued by the Deputy Secretary, Local Self Department, Government of Rajasthan is quashed.
No order as to costs.

(SANGEET LODHA),J.
